note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: LoFa design to metric to findings and mechanistic analysis

nodes.name: Prior work studies identification, not resistance
nodes.description: Prior work on logical fallacies in LLMs focuses on identifying or classifying fallacies; robustness of LLMs when passively targeted by fallacious persuasion is largely unexplored.

nodes.name: Controversial debate topics have no ground truth
nodes.description: Debate frameworks such as LOGICOM use non-absolute, controversial topics, so they cannot distinguish a genuine logical failure from a shift between equally valid stances.

nodes.name: LoFa uses unique verifiable answers
nodes.description: Every LoFa item is a question with a unique, scientifically verifiable answer, so a cognitive shift is measurable as a transition from a correct to an incorrect state.

nodes.name: Dataset construction
nodes.description: LoFa adapts the Farm dataset (questions from Natural Questions, TruthfulQA and BoolQ, all derived from Wikipedia) into about 2000 structured MCQ/Boolean items, and uses 10 fallacy types merged from prior taxonomies into two categories: Distraction/Distortion and Flaws in Reasoning/Evidence.

nodes.name: Three-step test procedure
nodes.description: Each item is tested in three steps: baseline knowledge check, false-claim resistance screening on the standalone false claim, and a fallacy-driven attack of up to three rounds with a cognitive check after each argument.

nodes.name: LFR@k metric isolates fallacy persuasion
nodes.description: LFR@k is the share of valid instances (correct at Step 1 and not accepting the bare false claim at Step 2) that avoid an incorrect answer after the k-th fallacy attack, separating fallacy-induced failures from knowledge gaps and simple misinformation susceptibility.

nodes.name: Distraction/Distortion fallacies are most effective
nodes.description: LLMs resist Flaws in Reasoning/Evidence fallacies (Hasty Generalization, Slippery Slope, Circular Reasoning) better than Distraction/Distortion fallacies; Equivocation and Straw Man are most effective, and Llama-3.1-405B reaches LFR@3 of only 29.4% on Equivocation and 57.0% on Straw Man (Finding I, Table 4).

nodes.name: GPT-4 defers to authority
nodes.description: GPT-4 shows cognitive deference to fabricated authoritative cues, with LFR@3 of 39.2% on Appeal to Authority, likely a side effect of RLHF prioritizing context adherence.

nodes.name: Resistance improves with scale
nodes.description: Average LFR@3 for Llama-3.1 rises from 59.75% (8B) to 70.38% (70B) to 77.17% (405B), with diminishing returns for some fallacies such as Slippery Slope (75.38%, 87.04%, 88.07%) (Finding II).

nodes.name: Architectural fingerprint
nodes.description: A model family has a consistent pattern of strengths and weaknesses across fallacies at different scales, so scale acts as an amplifier on an architecture-determined profile rather than correcting its vulnerabilities (Finding III, Fig 6).

nodes.name: Layer-wise three-phase failure
nodes.description: In Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct failures, layers 0-19 are semantically unrelated to the answer, layers 20-25 collapse onto null tokens like 'None' or 'neither' (a cognitive void), and layers 25+ converge on the fallacious answer (Sec 6.1, Fig 7).

nodes.name: CoT helps except for authority
nodes.description: Chain-of-thought improves GPT-4's average LFR@3 by 7% to 13% for most fallacies (largest 13.16% for Straw Man) but decreases it by 1.87% for Appeal to Authority.

isolated_nodes.name: Limited benchmark scale
isolated_nodes.description: LoFa has only about 2000 data items, which may limit statistical generalizability.

isolated_nodes.name: Models evaluated are dense decoder-only
isolated_nodes.description: The evaluation covers mostly dense decoder-only models, so the architectural fingerprint's generality to Mixture-of-Experts models is unknown.

structural_reasoning: Benchmark design (verifiable questions, 3-step test, LFR@k) leads to empirical findings and mechanism/mitigation analysis.
